architecture_decisions: One execution authority from PLAN through VERIFY
work_items: Protected PLAN already materializes the exact current accepted source lineage, binds one closed-catalog `ExecutionContract`, and persists its server-owned identity. That binding remains authoritative for the Engineering Run until an already-governed human-authorized PLAN refresh creates a new authoritative PLAN. Successful IMPLEMENT may create a new accepted source lineage, but it does not create a new execution contract or authorize source-shape reclassification. For an Engineering Run with accepted IMPLEMENT lineage, BUILD/TEST/VERIFY therefore require two independent authoritative references: 1. accepted source-lineage identity — determines exactly which source bytes execute; 2. PLAN-bound contract identity — determines exactly how those bytes execute. Neither may be inferred from the other after IMPLEMENT.
validations: Tests prove contract ID, binding reason, target, contract digest, validation-profile ID, and validation-profile digest must all match the server-resolved closed-catalog contract exactly.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — The authoritative record identifies exact deployment `dpl_6ahCYmgKUyaFCZJVAEB2cMfQNGMD`, QA run `33506848853` / job `99852814534`, Engineering Run `c7c6a645-aa4e-4440-b4d3-19ff1bbc8a82`, successful IMPLEMENT/source-lineage acceptance, and later `AUTONOMOUS_BUILD_FAILED`, closing #546 without claiming end-to-end success.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — For accepted IMPLEMENT lineage, BUILD/TEST/VERIFY receives the exact bounded execution-contract identity from authoritative successful PLAN evidence and no longer selects execution authority from post-IMPLEMENT source shape.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Tests prove contract ID, binding reason, target, contract digest, validation-profile ID, and validation-profile digest must all equal the server-resolved closed-catalog contract. Missing, malformed, unknown, or drifted identity fails closed.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — A deterministic regression reproduces post-IMPLEMENT source containing root `index.html`, `styles.css`, and `app.js` without generic ecosystem markers and proves a valid PLAN-bound `static-web-v1` contract reaches the existing server-owned static-web BUILD command instead of `UNSUPPORTED_VALIDATION_ECOSYSTEM`.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Tests prove adding `package.json`, Python markers, .NET project markers, or conflicting source-shape signals after PLAN cannot switch a `static-web-v1` same-lineage run to Node/Python/.NET commands or snapshots.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Tests prove wrong Project/run/lineage identity, file-set mismatch, symlink/special-file presence, byte/SHA mismatch, or aggregate lineage mismatch still fails before protected execution. Contract correctness cannot bypass source-lineage verification.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Focused regressions prove existing governed Python and .NET PLAN contracts resolve to the same profile/target/snapshot/preparation/command behavior and do not gain new authority.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Tests prove source-free snapshot verification, dependency preparation, validation-network lock, registered command policy, timeout, bounded evidence, and cleanup behavior remain authoritative after contract resolution.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Tests prove invalid contract evidence cannot persist raw exception text, source/generated content, provider payloads, filesystem roots, environment values, credentials, or true mutation/lineage/Git/deployment/REVIEW authority claims.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — SpecCritic/SpecCompiler evidence for this exact spec, focused regressions, full API regression, applicable client checks, protected promotion evaluation, Bounded Autonomy, Workstream Spec Validation, and exact-head PR gates are green.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — After exact merged API source reaches production `READY`, the real static-web candidate canary passes, `/health` and `/ready` are HTTP 200, and runtime verification is clean, rerun the authenticated marker-free QA path. Same-lineage BUILD must consume the persisted `static-web-v1` contract and advance to TEST/VERIFY/REVIEW or expose a genuinely later bounded blocker. Recurrence of source-shape `UNSUPPORTED_VALIDATION_ECOSYSTEM` or equivalent post-IMPLEMENT contract re-inference does not pass.
risks: Exact accepted-lineage Project/run identity, file set, byte size, per-file SHA-256, aggregate lineage evidence, sandbox source transfer, snapshot restoration, and cleanup verification remain mandatory.

critique: The later bounded `AUTONOMOUS_BUILD_FAILED` blocker exposed by authenticated P2-V0.23.33 production acceptance is the legacy post-IMPLEMENT source-shape re-inference that can contradict already-authoritative PLAN execution identity, while preserving exact accepted-lineage verification, closed-catalog execution profiles, source-free execution snapshots, dependency-preparation/network controls, command authority, mutation authority, provider/model/retry limits, Git/deployment/lifecycle authority, and the human REVIEW ceiling.
